name: Companion & Small Animals

objectives.text: Identify the basic needs of a pet, such as food, water, shelter, and exercise
Sort common animals into companion, farm, and wild animal groups and explain each choice
Describe the daily and weekly responsibilities of caring for a companion animal, including feeding schedules and cleaning its living space
Demonstrate calm, safe ways to approach, pick up, and hold a small animal such as a rabbit or guinea pig
Explain differences in the housing, dietary, and social needs of common companion mammals such as dogs, cats, and rabbits
Identify common breeds of dogs, cats, and rabbits by their visual characteristics
Demonstrate basic grooming tasks for a companion animal, including brushing, nail trimming, and bathing
Recommend an appropriate companion animal species or breed for a household by weighing its space, time, budget, and lifestyle
Compare the care requirements of exotic companion species such as reptiles, birds, and small rodents with those of dogs and cats
Identify common diseases and internal and external parasites of companion animals and the vaccines and preventive measures used against each
Compare the uses of companion animals as pets, service animals, therapy animals, and working animals
Use correct terminology for the sex, age, and breed classification of small animal species such as rabbits and cavies
Analyze pet food labels to compare guaranteed analysis, ingredient lists, and life-stage nutrition claims
Calculate daily feeding amounts for a companion animal based on its body weight, life stage, and activity level
Describe the housing and equipment requirements of small animals, including cage size, bedding, ventilation, and temperature
Explain identification and tracking methods for companion animals, such as microchips, tattoos, ear tags, and licensing
Evaluate a companion animal's behavior and body condition to identify signs of stress, illness, or poor welfare
Determine when a companion animal health concern must be referred to a veterinarian
Apply species-specific restraint and handling techniques for examining, grooming, and medicating small animals based on their behavior
Evaluate a small animal enclosure or kennel facility for space, sanitation, ventilation, and safety
Explain the reproductive cycle and breeding management of a small animal species such as rabbits, including gestation and kindling
Design a vaccination and parasite prevention program for a dog, cat, or rabbit across its life stages
Analyze a local animal shelter or rescue program to judge how well it prevents neglect and protects animal welfare
Develop a supervised agricultural experience plan for a companion animal enterprise such as rabbit production, grooming, or boarding, including a budget and record-keeping system
Design a small-animal care and enrichment program for a shelter or boarding facility that addresses health, behavior, housing, and adoption readiness

changes: Kept all six original objectives, rewording two slightly. The grade 6 objective now names companion mammals so it does not overlap the new exotic species objective. The grade 12 objective now includes housing. Added grade-appropriate competencies in eleven areas: animal classification, safe handling, breed identification, grooming, matching an animal to a household, exotic species care, and disease and parasite identification. The other new areas are pet food label analysis, ration calculation, housing requirements, and identification and tracking. Also added veterinary referral decisions, species-specific restraint, facility evaluation, rabbit reproduction, preventive health program design, shelter program analysis, and a companion animal SAE plan. Left welfare versus rights, careers, aquaculture, and animal products to the sibling sub-topics. Attached AFNR codes only to grade 9 to 12 objectives that directly teach them.
